title: Swedish crown slide seen quashing easing prospects.
text:
LONDON, March 14 (Reuter) - The flood of hot money out of the Swedish crown is set to continue, dampening chances of the rate cuts the central bank is keen to make, analysts say. 

 The crown slid to its worst levels in a year on Friday, in a sharp extension of the downtrend which has seen it shed more than six percent of its value against the mark since October. 

 Traders blamed speculative sales, mostly by foreign players. 

 "It's nothing to do with fundamentals because you couldn't pick a country with better economic fundamentals," said Keld Holm, international economist at Lehman Brothers in London. 

 The crown fell to a session low of 4.5790 per mark in afternoon Europe from Monday's close here around 4.5060/90. 

 Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said he was not worried by the soft crown. "With an inflation target and a floating crown this is something you have to be prepared for," he told journalists. 

 Traders said the market had taken this as a green light to sell more crowns -- though they doubted that was what Asbrink had intended. 

 "The government wants rates to go lower and with the crown this weak the Riksbank won't cut rates," said Peter Lindquist, Nordic economist at HSBC Markets in Stockholm. 

 The market has been particularly chary of the Swedish unit since January, when Prime Minister Goran Persson pledged to spend 10 billion crowns on public services, Lindquist said. 

 Markets, fearing Sweden's two-year programme of fiscal toughness had been ended in a bid to woo voters, punished the crown on hearing of the plans. 

 Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said this week that the crown was undervalued, but indicated that the currency had not yet reached a point where it had become a policy concern. 

 "The Swedish crown is easy to pick on -- the Riksbank doesn't have the same commitment as other central banks to keep intervening because it's not in the ERM (exchange rate mechanism)," said Lehman's Holm. 

 The Riksbank intervenes to smooth volatility rather than steer the crown, believing fundamentals will eventually drive it higher again, analysts said. 

 The weak crown has put the Riksbank in an awkward position. In January, deputy governor Lars Heikensten said the soft currency had contributed to the bank's decision not to cut its key interest rate, the repo, since December 17. 

 Until then, the bank had been easing frequently with 25 cuts from early 1996 when the the rate stood at 8.91 percent. 

 In fact, expectations are likely to lean towards tightening as Sweden's position outside the EMS makes open market intervention increasingly unsustainable, said Joe Prendergast, foreign exchange strategist at Merrill Lynch. 

 Yet that speculation, plus mild recovery prospects and high real rates, are unlikely to benefit the crown, he believed. 

 Insufficient fiscal progress and a lack of credible fiscal retrenchment plans for the near future are seen preventing Sweden participating in European monetary union, even in the event of stronger political will, said Prendergast.

title: FOCUS -  Intervention  powers Swedish crown to highs.
text:
STOCKHOLM, Oct 25 (Reuter) - Central Bank intervention catapulted the Swedish crown to new heights today and analysts said the currency is now on a roll. 

 "There is definitely a change in sentiment taking place... The crown is like a Spike Lee film, it is doing the right thing," said Andrew Bosomworth, an economist at Merrill Lynch. 

 The crown -- often seen as a peripheral currency along with the Spanish peseta and the Italian lira -- may now be on the way to 4.60 per mark. "Today's breakthrough means that the field is free for a move towards 4.60," said one forex dealer. 

 A move to 4.50 in the longer term is also seen possible. 

 "The level of 4.50 is not utopian by any means. We are in a positive trend and 4.50 within a year is not at all unthinkable," said Ake Gustafsson, economist at Swedbank. 

 The crown broke through a year high in early trade as the Swedish Riksbank moved in to offer support. It touched a high of 4.7130 against the mark before falling back to stand at 4.7370/00 by 1430 GMT compared with 4.7840 on Tuesday. 

 The crown was last trading as high as 4.60 on May 3, 1994. 

 Economists said that while basic economic problems remain for Sweden, still considered a high-yielder, today's Riksbank intervention served its purpose. 

 Sources said the Riksbank intervened repeatedly to push the strengthening crown to new highs. "The more people see the Riksbank intervening, the more optimistic they grow on the fundamentals," said Michael Dicks, an economist with J P Morgan. 

 Swedish inflation, the Riksbank's biggest enemy, has improved considerably in the past months, falling to 2.5 percent in September from 2.7 percent in August. 

 In April and May this year inflation was running above 3.0 percent, breaching the Riksbank target of 1-3 percent. 

 "Still, there are potential pressures," said Michael Dicks of J P Morgan. Among these are the fact that producer prices have risen more rapidly than consumer prices. 

 Economists also said the crown has been salvaged by Swedish export companies switching out of the weak dollar into crowns. 

 "What we are seeing now is being helped by export companies needing to cover short positions and by the Riksbank intervening. These are technical factors which are good for the crown," said Bosomworth of Merrill Lynch. 

 Some analysts feel 4.50 is the level where the Riksbank may choose to enter the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM). "If it can be sustained at that level, then they may choose to join," said one economist. 

 Before then, the Social Democratic government will have to prove it can continue to cut the budget and keep inflation low even in a period of stagnating growth, economists said. 

 Riksbank Governor Urban Backstrom said earlier the time was not right for Sweden to join the ERM. "The crown is still undervalued and it is therefore the wrong time for Sweden to join the ERM," he told a banking conference.
